summary.headline: Usha Martin Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore and EBITDA grew 44% to INR 208 crore at a 20.1% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 208 crore and margin up 380 bps YoY to 20.1%. Value grew faster than volume, driven by pass-through of input costs, a richer mix of value-added rope and plasticated LRPC, and a higher rope share. Wire rope volumes were marginally down as the Middle East fell about 28%, while India, the US and Europe grew. Operating cash flow was about INR 242 crore (116% of EBITDA), and free cash flow was INR 135 crore after INR 73 crore capex. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% rope volume growth and about 15% value growth, with a 20% minimum EBITDA margin base.

segments.name: Wire Rope
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18% YoY with value growth of 18% and marginally lower volumes; value-added rope share rose to 73% from 70% in FY26. Domestic rope volume up about 12% and value up about 21%. Middle East volume fell about 28% while realisations rose about 36%, holding revenue broadly flat.

segments.name: Wire and Strand (Wires)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 19% and revenue up about 32% YoY; largely domestic, with early European supply in automotive and rockfall protection. Wire realisation about INR 85,000 per ton.

segments.name: LRPC (black and plasticated)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3.9% YoY despite a volume decline; plasticated LRPC posted its highest volume and value to date. First international plasticated LRPC order for stay cable applications. Blended black and plasticated realisation about INR 79,000 per ton; management flagged some realisation softness from monsoon and project slowdowns.

segments.name: Oceanfibre (synthetic slings)
segments.commentary: Revenue has trended up for five consecutive quarters, now about GBP 2-3 million per year with a GBP 10 million target over the next few years. Gross margin 65-70%; estimated TAM INR 1.5-2 billion.

guidance_outlook: Rope volume growth of 10-12% and value growth of about 15% for FY27, conditional on the Middle East situation not worsening; management said it expects the same growth pace in coming years.
EBITDA margin floor of 20%, with quarterly variation within 20-21% and upside from capacity and mix; no margin-per-ton guidance.
Plasticated LRPC FY27 volume target of 3,500-4,000 tons against 6,000 tons annual capacity, versus about 2,500 tons in FY26.
FY27 capex of INR 250-300 crore, which management said is also the annual run-rate needed for 10-12% volume and about 15% value growth.
Thailand and UM Cables plan to be defined within 2-3 quarters; management is evaluating integrating Thailand with India operations.
capex_capacity: Elevator rope capacity expansion of about 6,000 metric tons per annum, commissioning in phases from October 2026, completion by Q1 FY28.
Furnace modernisation and expansion to meet higher demand.
Plasticated LRPC: front-end capacity exists for 6,000 tons; only the plastification line needs additional capex, and management is considering further expansion within 18-24 months.
Management said elevator rope is capacity constrained in India, with the market growing about 20%.
demand_pricing: Middle East volumes fell about 28% (roughly 1,000 tons in the quarter per management) due to the conflict, with project delays in Saudi Arabia and conservative distributor stocking; the region is about 9% of revenue.
Asia Pacific saw project-related delays, which management described as deferred rather than lost demand.
Europe contributed about 27% of revenue, and the US/Americas about 9-10%; US market share is below 5% and Europe about 10-12%.

Steel prices rose about INR 7,000 per ton (about 13% QoQ); wire rod prices were about 7% higher YoY and zinc about 28% higher. Management said 100% of commodity input increases have been passed through.
Realisations: domestic rope about INR 1,90,000 per ton; international rope INR 3,70,000-3,80,000 per ton (mix-dependent).

qa_highlights.question: How much volume loss came from the Middle East, and what is the outlook for rope volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rope volumes were marginally lower, with Middle East down about 28% and Asia Pacific seeing project delays. It reiterated 10-12% volume growth for FY27, conditional on the global situation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and how much did LRPC pricing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management set a minimum 20% margin base, with quarterly variation in a 20-21% range from product and geographic mix. It said all steel, gas and input cost increases were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise only about 3% QoQ when steel rose about 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel increase is about INR 7,000 per ton in absolute terms and is recovered in full; it is not a percentage applied to finished-product prices. EBITDA per ton was INR 40,581.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oceanfibre TAM and why are margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: The TAM is estimated at INR 1.5-2 billion and gross margins are 65-70%. The products are specialised heavy-lifting slings for oil, offshore and wind, where steel rope cannot be used, and they need approvals and track record.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plasticated LRPC volume outlook and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: A major domestic-share customer approval was verbally confirmed with paperwork pending. FY27 target is 3,500-4,000 tons against 2,500 tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for UM Cables and Thailand, which are loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: UM Cables is non-core and may be repurposed for value-added wire and rope; management does not want to remain in cables long term. Thailand margins improved and a plan is expected within 6 months, possibly integrating it with India.

financial_highlights.change: +380 bps YoY; moderated sequentially per management
